A homozygote variant is when an individual has two identical gene copies for a specific trait or gene, either both normal or both mutated.
A heterozygote is an individual with two different gene copies for a specific trait or gene, typically one normal and one mutated.
a wildetype variant.
A hemizygote is an individual with only one copy of a gene in a diploid organism, typically found in sex chromosomes (e.g., males having one X and one Y chromosome).

terms.display: Typified by highly variable age of onset
terms.description: Description of conditions in which age of onset is highly variable even in family members who share the same disease-associated variant or variants.

A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on chromosomes in which a trait can manifest in a monoallelic (e.g. heterozygotes) and biallelic (e.g. homozygotes, compound heterozygotes) state, with similar or differing phenotype severity present dependent on the number of alleles affected.
A mode of inheritance that depends on genetic determinants in more than one gene
A type of multifactorial inheritance governed by the simultaneous action of two gene loci
A mode of inheritance that depends on a mixture of major and minor genetic determinants possibly together with environmental factors. Diseases inherited in this manner are termed complex diseases

A type of multifactorial inheritance governed by the simultaneous action of a few gene loci. It is recommended this term be used for traits governed by three loci, although it is noted that usage of this term in the literature is not uniform
Cases of the disease in question occur without a previous family history, i.e., as isolated cases without being transmitted from a parent and without other siblings being affected
Genes with indeterminate inheritance patterns
Moderate proportion of individuals exhibit the disease (20-80%)
Low proportion of individuals exhibit the disease (less than 20%)
Hight proportion of individuals exhibit the disease (80-100%)

Imprinting is a natural process where one parent's gene copy is silenced during development, leaving only one active. In diseases linked to imprinting, the disorder usually appears when a harmful variant is inherited from the normally active parent, but not when it's from the silenced parent.

terms.display: Autosomal dominant inheritance with maternal imprinting
terms.description: A type of autosomal dominant inheritance involving a gene that is imprinted with maternal silencing

terms.description: A type of autosomal dominant inheritance involving a gene that is imprinted with paternal silencing

A type of autosomal dominant inheritance involving a gene that exhibits anticipation, the increase in severity and/or an earlier age of onset in subsequent generations

A likely pathogenic variant, as per the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines, is a genetic alteration with a strong probability of causing a specific disease or condition. While not confirmed as definitively pathogenic, these variants are strongly associated with the observed clinical symptoms and play a significant role in medical genetics for diagnosis and treatment considerations.

An uncertain significance variant, following the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines, is a genetic alteration for which the potential impact on health is not definitively determined.

A likely benign variant, in accordance with the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines, is a genetic alteration with a high probability of being non-pathogenic and not causing a specific disease or condition.

A benign variant, following the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines, is a genetic alteration that has been determined to have no adverse impact on an individual's health.

A pathogenic variant, as defined by the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines, is a genetic alteration that is associated with a high likelihood of causing a specific disease or condition.
